episode.tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
episode.title: Chatbot or AI Agent: What Is the Difference?

onScreen.text: An AI agent can send 500 emails while you sleep.
onScreen.emphasis: But what if it sends the wrong information?

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: An AI agent can send five hundred emails while you sleep.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: But what happens when it sends the wrong information?

onScreen.title: Chatbot or AI Agent?
onScreen.subtitle: What is the difference, and why it matters for your business

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Welcome to the AI Workshop. Today: chatbot, or AI agent. What is the difference?

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Tanyi, I asked our chatbot to schedule an interview with a candidate. It gave me a nice list of steps. But nothing happened.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Right. That is the whole difference in one sentence. The chatbot answered you. It did not act for you.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A chatbot reads your message, writes an answer, and stops. That is useful, but it is passive.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: An AI agent works toward a goal. It can reason, use tools, remember context, and take actions. But only within the permissions you give it.

onScreen.title: Same request, given to an agent

messages.text: Schedule a 30 minute interview with Amina next week.
On it. Checking the calendar first.

ui.subject: Interview: Tuesday 10:00
body: Could you join us Tuesday at 10:00 for a 30 minute interview?

steps.title: Waits for human approval
steps.detail: Nothing is sent until a person says yes.

ui.title: Kito wants to send an email

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Kito, schedule a thirty minute interview with Amina next week.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Checking the calendar. Tuesday at ten is free.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Drafting the invitation to Amina now. Interview, Tuesday at ten, thirty minutes.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: Nothing goes out until a human approves it. Approved. That is how it should be.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Notice what Kito did. First, a goal.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Then reasoning: it planned the steps.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Then tools: the calendar and the email.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Then action, but only with permission. Those four parts turn a chatbot into an agent.

onScreen.title: Before an agent acts, ask:
items: What is it allowed to do?

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: An agent that can act, can also act wrongly. Give it the smallest permissions it needs.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: And keep a human in the loop for anything that sends, pays, or deletes.

onScreen.emphasis: Pick one task you repeat every week. Write down its goal, the tools it needs, and who should approve the result.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Here is one thing to try today. Pick one task you repeat every week. Write down its goal, the tools it needs, and who should approve the result. That is your first agent design.

onScreen.cta: Subscribe for the next episode: Why AI Hallucinates

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Don't just use AI. Build it to work reliably. See you in the next episode.

tanyi.name: Tanyi
tanyi.role: AI engineer and instructor, the animated host. Middle-aged Black African man. Calm, direct, practical. Has built and operated real systems.

amara.name: Amara
amara.role: Curious learner who asks the questions beginners are thinking.

kito.name: Kito
kito.role: Small AI assistant who demonstrates concepts and occasionally makes believable mistakes.

hallucinator.name: The Hallucinator
hallucinator.role: Mischievous. Represents confident but incorrect AI output.

gatekeeper.name: The Gatekeeper
gatekeeper.role: Represents security, privacy, governance and human approval.
